nodes.title: Keep the selected chips in a signal
nodes.why: chips holds every invited person and custom entry, and suggestions reads it to hide people who are already invited, so each add or removal has to reach the signal.
nodes.alternative: A plain Chip[] field changed with push and splice and read through getters on every change detection pass.
nodes.tradeoff: Every edit must hand the signal a new array through update, but the suggestion list and the OnPush view see each one.

nodes.title: Derive suggestions with computed
nodes.why: It filters users by name or email, skips ids already in chips and caps the list at six; it reruns only when query or chips change, and handleKeyDown reads the same cached list as the template.
nodes.alternative: A getter that rebuilds the filtered array on each change detection pass and again on every keydown.
nodes.tradeoff: A computed only notices signal reads, so the users list must stay constant or become a signal, while repeated reads within one pass cost nothing.

nodes.title: Reject duplicates by id or normalized value
nodes.why: addChip compares ids and trimmed lowercase values, so typing zed CUSTOM with stray spaces adds nothing when Zed Custom exists, and the query still clears.
nodes.alternative: Compare raw labels, which lets casing and extra spaces produce repeated chips for the same person.
nodes.tradeoff: Normalizing on each comparison is cheap for a few chips, and custom text equal to a user's email counts as that user, which is the intended match.

nodes.title: Let Enter pick a suggestion or create a chip
nodes.why: Enter adds the highlighted suggestion when the list is open and an option is active; otherwise addCustomFromQuery turns the typed text into a custom chip.
nodes.alternative: Accept only suggestions on Enter and offer a separate button for inviting an address that is not in the list.
nodes.tradeoff: One key covers both paths, but after Escape closes the list, Enter creates a custom chip from the text even if an option was highlighted before.

nodes.title: Remove the last chip only from an empty input
nodes.why: Backspace erases typed text first; only when the query is already empty does it drop the most recent chip, by slicing it off the end of the array.
nodes.alternative: Remove a chip on every Backspace, which deletes invites while the user is still fixing a typo in the input.
nodes.tradeoff: Keydown fires before the input updates, so deleting the last letter and removing a chip take separate presses, which is how tag inputs usually behave.

nodes.title: Close the list on presses outside the field
nodes.why: The document-level mouse-down listener in the host metadata closes the list and resets activeIndex only when the press lands outside this component, so pressing an option still adds it.
nodes.alternative: Close the list on input blur, which runs before a click on an option and can remove the option before the pick lands.
nodes.tradeoff: Listening on the whole document runs this check for every press on the page, a small cost for dismissal without blur timing races.
